extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, their counsel, and USPTO disciplinary/enforcement staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for an affidavit of resignation/consent to exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and related obligations (publication, compliance, and reinstatement consequences) for practitioners before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has authority to approve a respondent's affidavit and to exclude the respondent on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority is exercised pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27. The Director receives the affidavit from the OED Director for review and approval under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent practitioner is subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related disciplinary procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent (a registered patent attorney) is subject to 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq., which governs professional conduct and provides the regulatory framework for disciplinary actions and exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit of resignation submitted for exclusion on consent must comply with the specific requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director determined the respondent's affidavit 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' The affidavit should therefore contain the elements required by that regulation (see the following entries enumerating those elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent must be freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must state that the respondent's consent to exclusion is freely and voluntarily rendered, without coercion or duress, and that the respondent is aware of the implications of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered. He is not being subjected to coercion or duress. He is fully aware of the implications of consenting to exclusion.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must acknowledge awareness of pending proceedings/allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must acknowledge that there are pending disciplinary proceedings and/or investigations and describe the nature of the allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the order: respondent acknowledged awareness of a pending disciplinary proceeding under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 alleging violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) (predicated on a conviction) and a pending investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 alleging violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) (predicated on disbarment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant may deny legal conclusions but must acknowledge reinstatement presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the respondent denies the legal conclusion of misconduct, the affidavit must acknowledge that for purposes of any future reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 the OED Director will conclusively presume the underlying facts are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'He denies the legal conclusion that he violated either 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) or 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1). Nonetheless, he acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume at that time, and for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that the facts ... are true, and that he could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations ...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiant must consent to being excluded from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit must include an explicit consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non‑patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text (summarized): respondent 'consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.' The Final Order then orders exclusion to commence on the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of affidavit resolves pending disciplinary proceeding and investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of an affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent resolves the pending disciplinary proceeding and the pending investigation identified in the affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'This Final Order resolves Respondent's pending disciplinary proceeding... and pending investigation...' Acceptance of the affidavit is the mechanism for resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director must publish Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is required to electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room, which is publicly accessible at http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice must be published and materially consistent with provided text
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of the exclusion on consent must be published in the Official Gazette and be materially consistent with the sample notice text provided in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs: 'The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: Notice of Exclusion on Consent...' and includes the full sample text describing the respondent, the acceptance of the affidavit, nature of allegations, denial of legal conclusions, and statutory/regulatory citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent excluded on consent must comply fully with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58;' (Section 11.58 contains the duties and notices required of excluded or suspended practitioners; the order imposes compliance as a condition of the exclusion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the excluded respondent seeks reinstatement, the respondent must comply fully with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page text: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' The affidavit also acknowledged that the OED Director will apply the reinstatement presumptions described in § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline referenced: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) and § 11.804(h)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order identifies specific disciplinary grounds alleged: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) (predicated on a criminal conviction) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) (predicated on disbarment by a state supreme court).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language: allegations of misconduct 'the nature of which is the allegation that he violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) predicated on a judgment of conviction ...' and '... violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) predicated on his disbarment from the Supreme Court of New Jersey.' These rules provide bases for USPTO discipline.
